The expected validation primary is ~0.6016. This establishes the pipeline for all future iterations.

I want to understand the data distribution, feature statistics, and interaction patterns that will guide feature engineering decisions. Specifically: how many unique videos/users appear in each split, the long_view rate by tab/duration/time features, user engagement variance, and what temporal patterns exist. This will tell me whether time-of-day features, user history features, or video-side aggregations are most promising, and calibrate expected gains against the noise floor.

Training N=3 FM models on different seeds (args.seed, args.seed+1, args.seed+2), converting each model's scores to within-user fractional ranks, and averaging those ranks will outperform a single-seed FM by at least 0.002 on the primary metric.
mechanism: GAUC and nDCG@5 are both pure ranking metrics - only the ordering within each user's list matters. Rank averaging reduces variance in the rank estimates: when two models disagree on the relative order of two items, the average rank reflects the ensemble's uncertainty. This variance reduction is larger than any bias introduced, especially for users with few impressions (~5 median), where a single model's ranking can be flipped by initialization noise. Within-user rank normalization ensures the average is in comparable units across users.

evidence.task_structure: With median 5 impressions per user and a binary label, ranking two items correctly requires the score difference to exceed noise - averaging ranks across 3 random initializations reduces this noise. 57.8% of users are 'mixed' and contribute to GAUC; each one benefits from reduced ordering variance.
evidence.previous_experiments: The findings section explicitly states: 'Seed ensembling with within-user rank averaging: +0.0016. Averaging raw scores gave about half as much; the rank-space step is where most of it came from.' History table shows ensembling has 55% accept rate, median +0.0019, best +0.0024 across 9 attempts.
evidence.literature: No search results were directly relevant to rank averaging for within-user ranking.

proposed_change: Train 3 FM models with seeds [args.seed, args.seed+1, args.seed+2], each with early stopping on validation primary. For each model, convert raw scores to within-user fractional ranks (scipy.stats.rankdata per user). Average the fractional ranks across 3 models. Use averaged ranks as the final score.

falsification_condition: VAL_PRIMARY <= 0.6034 (less than +0.002 above baseline) would indicate the ensemble gain is inside the noise floor for N=3 seeds.

risks.overfitting: Low - ensembling reduces, not increases, overfitting.

The history table shows ensembling is the most reliable mechanism (55% accept rate, median +0.0019, best +0.0024). hypothesis: Adding Bayesian-smoothed per-video and per-author long_view rates (computed from training data, smoothed toward global rate, bucketed into 5 bins) as new features to the FM ensemble will improve validation primary by ~0.0008 on top of the current 0.6022, reaching ~0.6030
mechanism: Video CTR rate and author CTR rate vary across the 5 candidate videos shown to a user (unlike pure user-level stats which cancel), so they provide discriminative signal inside each user's impression set. Bayesian smoothing prevents overfitting on rare items. Bucketing makes them usable in the FM's embedding table. The FM can learn cross-terms between user embedding and the CTR bucket, capturing 'user X tends to watch videos from popular/unpopular categories'.

evidence.task_structure: Validation has ~5 impressions per user; all scoring is within-user. Video CTR rate varies across those 5 videos, so it provides ordering signal. 57.8% of users are mixed-label, so this signal can actually affect GAUC. Per-video statistics computed from 1.14M training rows give reliable estimates for the 6457 videos with >10 impressions (covering most validation impressions).
evidence.previous_experiments: Established findings section explicitly states: 'Bayesian-smoothed per-video and per-author long_view rate, bucketed: +0.0008' and 'Those two together account for +0.0024 of a best-ever +0.0025, and they compose: the ensembling result was measured on top of the smoothed-CTR model'. Node 2 already has the ensembling (+0.0006 in this run), so adding CTR features should compound.
evidence.literature: Search returned [W2962745591] Deep Interest Evolution Network - confirms CTR history features are useful for ranking but does not directly address Bayesian smoothing for item-level statistics. Not directly applicable.

proposed_change: Compute per-video and per-author Bayesian-smoothed long_view rates from training rows only. Smooth formula: rate = (sum_lv + alpha) / (count + alpha/global_rate) where alpha=5 (prior count equivalent). Bucket each into 5 equal-frequency bins using training distribution. Add these two bucketed columns as new FM features alongside the existing 5 FIELDS, increasing X from 5 columns to 7 columns. Keep everything else identical to node 2 (3-seed ensemble, within-user rank averaging, early stopping).
expected_result: +0.0008 on top of 0.6022, reaching ~0.6030. Combined effect should be ~+0.0014 from baseline per established findings, potentially reaching 0.6030+.
falsification_condition: If VAL_PRIMARY < 0.6022 or the gain is under 0.001, the smoothed CTR features are not contributing meaningfully beyond what the video_id/author_id embeddings already capture, confirming the cold-start argument (only 0.01% cold-start in validation).

risks.leakage: Must compute CTR only from training rows, never including the row being scored. Using train split rows only — date-sliced before validation. No leakage risk if implemented correctly.
risks.overfitting: Bayesian smoothing mitigates overfitting on rare items. Risk is low since we're bucketing into 5 bins and the FM regularizes with l2=1e-6.
risks.runtime: Minimal overhead — precomputing CTR statistics is O(N_train). No change to model architecture or training loop.

Switch to pairwise/LambdaRank objective — history shows 18% accept rate, median -0.0014, too risky

The established findings explicitly state that Bayesian-smoothed video/author CTR bucketed features gave +0.0008, and combined with ensembling gave +0.0024 total from baseline. The current best (node 2) already has ensembling; adding smoothed CTR features is the one atomic change that was measured to compose with it.

hypothesis: Replacing pointwise BCE with BPR pairwise loss (sampling positive/negative pairs within each user per minibatch) will improve GAUC and nDCG@5 by directly optimizing the ranking criterion rather than a surrogate
mechanism: GAUC measures per-user AUC = P(score(pos) > score(neg)) for pairs within the same user. BPR loss minimizes -log(sigmoid(score_pos - score_neg)) over within-user pairs, which is exactly a differentiable proxy for 1-GAUC. With ~5 impressions per user and ~22k users in validation, the within-user pairs are informative signal that pointwise loss ignores by treating each row independently.

evidence.task_structure: Evaluation is within-user ranking over ~5 items; GAUC directly measures pairwise ranking accuracy within users; BPR loss is the natural objective for this metric
evidence.previous_experiments: Ranking objectives have best delta +0.0026 across prior runs (5/27 accepted), suggesting the mechanism can work when implemented correctly; node 3 baseline uses pointwise BCE which does not directly target the ranking criterion
evidence.literature: [W2963655167] VBPR confirms BPR pairwise loss with FM-style embeddings for implicit feedback ranking; the loss is -log(sigmoid(z_pos - z_neg)) summed over within-user positive/negative pairs

proposed_change: Implement BPR pairwise loss: for each minibatch, group rows by user, sample one positive and one negative per user who has both in the batch, compute FM scores for both, apply -log(sigmoid(z_pos - z_neg)) loss, update embeddings via Adam. Keep same features as node 3 (7 fields including smoothed CTR buckets), same 3-seed ensemble with rank averaging.
expected_result: +0.002 to +0.005 improvement in validation primary; the direct alignment between loss and metric should help especially GAUC
falsification_condition: If val_primary <= 0.6034 + 0.002 = 0.6054 after training, the pairwise objective did not help beyond noise; if train-val gap widens significantly (>0.10) the model is overfitting

risks.leakage: None: BPR only uses the label for pairing positive/negative within the batch, no cross-row statistics
risks.overfitting: Pairwise sampling within small user batches could overfit if users have very few impressions; mitigate by keeping same regularization (l2=1e-6) and early stopping
risks.runtime: BPR requires within-user pair sampling per batch which adds overhead, but with batch_size=8192 and ~26k users this should remain under 25 minutes for 3 seeds

candidates_considered: Increase ensemble size from 3 to 5 seeds: expected ~+0.0005, likely below noise floor given diminishing returns already seen

The model uses pointwise BCE loss but is evaluated on ranking metrics (GAUC, nDCG@5). The gap to oracle is ~0.26. The next lever is the training objective itself.
